name: TPU-LW

summary.text: TPU-LW is a foaming thermoplastic polyurethane, a lightweight flexible elastomer. Makers sell it for footwear, weight-saving drone and robot parts, and flexible wearables. Printed flat, it typically reaches a tensile strength of 10.3 MPa and breaks at 629 % elongation. On the H2C every product calls for drying, and makers warn of stringing and oozing as the foam expands in the hotend.

Upon Opening Immediately place the spool in a filament dryer or a sealed container with plenty of active desiccant.
Print directly from the dry box if possible.
TPU Air is hygroscopic (absorbs moisture), which severely impacts foaming and print quality, causing bubbles, stringing, and poor layer adhesion.
Immediately place the spool in a filament dryer or a sealed container with plenty of active desiccant (aim for <15% humidity).
Always store the spool back in the provided resealable bag with the desiccant pack, ensuring it's tightly sealed.
If you suspect moisture exposure, dry the filament thoroughly in a convection oven at 70°C - 80°C for 4-6 hours before printing.
(A filament dryer is not recommended because heating cannot maintain a uniform temperature throughout the entire environment.)
Always print in a well-ventilated area.
It is important to dial in flow rate as it is related to the temperature and how much the tpu air expanded as well as the flow rate of the extruder.

Models designed with continuous extrusion paths (minimal jumping between features) will yield the cleanest results due to reduced oozing.
If prints bond too strongly (especially on PEI), use a release agent like PVP glue stick, Magigoo, or even a light mist of Windex before printing.

items.text: Ketones such as acetone, methylethylketone (MEK) and cyclohexanone are partial solvents for thermoplastic polyurethane elastomers. Elastollan products are unsuitable for long-term use in these solvents. Methyl ethyl ketone: volume swelling 105 % / 110 % / 130 %, reduction of tensile strength 80 % / 80 % / 90 % (ester / C 85 A / ether); other short-chained aliphatic ketones such as acetone have a similar effect.

items.text: Aliphatic alcohols, such as ethanol and isopropanol, cause swelling of Elastollan products. This is combined with a loss of tensile strength. items.text: No reduction in strength occurs after immersion in test oils IRM 901, IRM 902, and IRM 903 at room temperature. There is also no reduction in tensile strength after 3 weeks immersion at 100 °C. Elastollan is in principal resistant to lubricating oils and greases, however irreversible damage can be caused by included additives. Compatibility testing in each individual lubricant is to be recommended.

items.text: Contact of Elastollan with saturated hydrocarbons such as diesel oil, isooctane, petroleum ether and kerosene results in a limited swelling. At room temperature, this swelling amounts to approx. 1-3 % and the resultant reduction in tensile strength is no more than 20 %. After evaporation and reversal of the swelling, the original mechanical properties are almost completely restored.

items.agent: Hot water, moisture vapour, tropical climate (polyester-based TPU)
items.text: If polyester based polyurethanes are exposed for lengthy periods to hot water, moisture vapor or tropical climates, an irreversible break-down of the polyester chains occurs through hydrolysis. This results in a reduction in mechanical properties. This effect is more marked in flexible grades. Due to a good stabilization, a degradation of polyester-based Elastollan is rarely experienced at room temperature.

items.text: Plastics are chemically degraded by the effect of UV radiation. The degree of ageing depends on duration and intensity. In the case of polyurethanes, the effect is seen initially as surface embrittlement. This is accompanied by a yellowing in color and a reduction in mechanical properties. It is possible to improve UV resistance by addition of color pigments which prevent the deep penetration of UV rays... The ageing process can also be delayed by the addition of UV stabilizers.
